topic: Rare-exceedance cancellation geometry for normal-link distributional DiD. For the fifteen fixed pre/post pairs in the Djuazon--Tsyawo crime-free DTT aggregate, use predeclared disjoint block-role samples and write each of four exceedance probabilities as rho c_j on a fixed comparable-rarity box. Prove that the complete probit-versus-Poisson error factors as rho Q A C_rho, where A=log(c1/c3)log(c2/c3), C_rho<0, and u^2 C_rho=-1+O(u^-2) uniformly including the exact cancellation planes. Derive the pairwise and aggregate drifting-cancellation Gaussian frontier, bounded-count product-Poisson limits, and a zero-count-safe finitely terminating rational outer confidence interval with simultaneous coverage and the stated expected-diameter order. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: An explicit inverse-Mills integral remainder yields the uniform mixed-derivative expansion without dividing by A. Exact-plane, opposite-sign, approaching-plane, all-zero, all-full, unequal-share, and fifteen-pair cases were checked. A rational-grid construction with an explicit global Lipschitz certificate preserves coverage and diameter order; bounded searches found no same-theorem collision. The published 37-treated-block sample forces the conservative aggregate interval to include zero, so no finite-sample power claim is made. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently prove the common-cutoff inverse-tail and mixed-derivative constants uniformly over the full coefficient box, closing K4-U on both cancellation planes. EARLY KILL TEST: Certify the mixed derivative as one log ratio tends to zero and verify all-zero retention plus the all-full empty-list output for n_j at most six; failure should pivot or stop. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/panel_rarelink_cancellation.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish a cancellation-safe uniform expansion for the normal-link versus Poisson distributional-DiD map on p_j = ρc_j, proving that its complete error is ρQAC_ρ with A = log(c_1/c_3)log(c_2/c_3), C_ρ < 0, and u²C_ρ = -1 + O(u⁻²), including both exact cancellation planes.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The available distributional-DiD delta method assumes that the working-link density is bounded away from zero, which fails for p_j = ρc_j under the normal link. Mills-ratio results give one-dimensional tail control, but not a uniform mixed finite-difference expansion when either log ratio is exactly or nearly zero. The prior binary-DiD scale proposal also records that its probit exhibit was false. The missing proof step is therefore a common-cutoff inverse-tail remainder that controls the mixed derivative over the full coefficient box without dividing by A.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform mixed-integral-remainder theorem on a fixed compact c-box giving the exact ρQAC_ρ factorization, strict negativity of C_ρ, and an explicit uniform u²C_ρ = -1 + O(u⁻²) expansion on and near both cancellation planes.

method_exemplars.why_closest: The coefficient C_ρ is governed by derivatives of the inverse Gaussian tail, exactly the analytic objects bounded by this paper.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt complete-monotonicity and Turán-type Mills-ratio inequalities to certify the mixed derivative's sign throughout the coefficient box.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Interior distributional-DiD theory does not cover the exploding inverse-normal derivative. Existing second-order delta methods address a vanishing derivative while retaining a Gaussian base experiment, whereas bounded expected exceedance counts generate a discrete product-Poisson experiment. Neither line gives a frontier jointly indexed by nρ_n and two drifting log ratios or propagates that frontier through the fixed dependence and weights of fifteen pair-specific contrasts. Prior reviewers independently identified the absence of an observable statistic and limit law as a decisive gap.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A triangular-array theorem specifying the normalization and joint law of every pair and their fixed weighted aggregate across Gaussian, cancellation-degenerate Gaussian, product-Poisson, and exact-zero regimes, with explicit boundary conditions.

writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Distributional DiD aggregates valid comparisons -> interior inference is Gaussian -> rarity and cancellation suppress ordinary first order -> a regime-indexed Gaussian/Poisson frontier is required.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the second-order Hadamard expansion and modified-bootstrap argument for functionals with a vanishing first derivative.
method_exemplars.why_closest: On a cancellation plane the link-discrepancy functional is first-order degenerate in the diverging-count regime.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The available block bootstrap is unjustified when the normal inverse-link derivative diverges or an empirical probability equals zero or one. General multinomial-function intervals exist, but their nuisance optimization does not supply a deterministic rational certificate, global discretization error, or the desired rare-regime diameter theorem. The prior weak-count verifier explicitly excludes equality contacts and a uniform finite cover; exact probit-versus-Poisson cancellation planes are precisely such contacts. A grid construction therefore requires a global rational Lipschitz and tail-error ledger rather than sampled numerical evidence.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A total algorithm returning rational endpoints and a finite certificate, with a theorem proving simultaneous coverage, finite termination, all-zero retention, all-full empty-list behavior, and the stated uniform expected-diameter bound.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from bootstrap failure for nonlinear discrete-probability functionals to guaranteed-coverage inversion.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Causal targets are nonlinear functions of cell probabilities -> delta and bootstrap inference fail near boundaries -> finite-sample inversion restores coverage -> specialize and certify inversion for the rare distributional-DiD aggregate.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt finite sample-space enumeration and worst-case null inversion, replacing stochastic nuisance search by a rational grid with a proved Lipschitz envelope.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its functional class contains the link-discrepancy contrast, while the proposed theorem adds deterministic certification.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Disjoint roles yield independent Poisson totals, but the original panel reuses the same blocks and months across multiple comparisons. One exceedance can therefore affect several contrasts, and that dependence remains first-order when counts are bounded. The prior weak-count construction explicitly relies on independent totals and excludes individual-data sufficiency. The first changed proof step is a marked dependency-graph or incidence representation of block-by-month exceedances, followed by propagation of its multivariate or compound-Poisson law through the cancellation-degenerate link map.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A dependency-graph theorem giving an explicit multivariate or compound-Poisson approximation for overlapping role counts, its covariance or Lévy measure, the induced pairwise and aggregate limit law, and a simultaneous interval with a diameter comparison to disjoint splitting.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode block-month exceedances by dependency neighborhoods and apply Chen-Stein process approximation with explicit total-variation error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Overlapping role counts are sums of locally dependent rare indicators, the canonical structure of this theorem.

method_exemplars.why_closest: The fifteen role samples can have unequal probabilities and shares even before overlap is introduced.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a zero-count-safe rare-link distributional-DiD interval retain uniform coverage and its target expected-diameter order when the common rarity intensity ρ is unknown or estimated rather than calibrated?

source_refs.excerpt: An unknown or estimated intensity changes the experiment and remains unsolved.
add an unknown-intensity or estimated-exposure extension as a clearly separated attainable regime.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The banked weak-count construction conditions on a known Poisson intensity; its zero-table probabilities, tail budgets, and connected-interval optimization all use that calibration. Estimating ρ introduces nuisance fluctuation that can be of the same order as a drifting cancellation signal, so naive plug-in calibration need not preserve simultaneous coverage or the expected-diameter rate.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit interval using auxiliary or jointly estimated ρ, with a uniform coverage theorem and matching expected-diameter bound across bounded-count, transition, and Gaussian rarity regimes, including the all-zero table and both cancellation planes.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert exact Poisson probabilities by finite enumeration to obtain short intervals that remain defined at zero counts.

method_exemplars.technique: Prove uniform size by reducing arbitrary parameter sequences to drifting subsequences and analyzing each limit experiment.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The common-cutoff proof represents all inverse Gaussian tails as small perturbations of one cutoff. With unequal α_j, cutoff differences are of the same order as the cutoff itself, so the mixed-derivative expansion and factor A no longer apply. Existing unequal-probability Poisson approximations do not analyze the nonlinear normal-link DiD composition, and the searched literature contains no phase diagram for this target-method pair.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A piecewise asymptotic characterization indexed by (α_1, α_2, α_3, α_4), specifying the leading power of ρ, sign, cancellation hypersurfaces, and associated Gaussian or Poisson sampling limits.

writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Distributional DiD combines four probabilities -> sparse cells need not vanish comparably -> common-tail expansions can fail -> map the unequal-rarity regimes.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply inverse-Mills bounds separately at the four α_j-dependent cutoffs and compare their leading scales before composing the DiD map.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proof needs certified control at widely separated Gaussian quantiles.

method_exemplars.why_closest: The observational cells are Bernoulli sums with probabilities differing by powers of ρ.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Transformation-invariance results concern transformations of the outcome rather than inverse-CDF links inside a distributional-DiD counterfactual operator. Nonlinear-DiD work identifies link choice as observationally underdetermined, while the distributional-DiD paper compares links without giving a tail classification. The missing object is a primitive tail-score condition that determines the leading discrepancy, sign, and cancellation order for normal, logistic, complementary-log-log, and other admissible links.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient characterization in terms of the inverse link's asymptotic logarithmic derivative near zero, with corollaries giving each standard link's leading discrepancy, sign, and cancellation order.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior weak-event proposal explicitly leaves selection honesty open. Maximizing over thresholds, projections, or admissible pairs couples the selected rarity probability, cancellation factor, and variance estimate. Pointwise inversion therefore omits both search multiplicity and the instability of models selected near a cancellation plane.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A simultaneous cell-inversion or confidence-sequence construction over a finite or complexity-controlled family, with uniform post-selection coverage and an expected-diameter bound in terms of rarity, cancellation distance, and family complexity.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt cross-fitted causal-score construction and studentized moment inversion to a simultaneous family of rare binary events.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The selected-threshold problem requires simultaneous rather than pointwise score inversion.

method_exemplars.technique: Approximate expected-size confidence-region optimization by finite games while certifying risk between grid points.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A finite threshold and pair family can be encoded as a larger action game, with off-grid control when thresholds vary continuously.

literature_map:
Djuazon and Tsyawo (2026, arXiv:2408.07842) identify distributional and quantile DiD effects for non-continuous outcomes through a three-input working-link counterfactual and apply it to crime-free probabilities over fifteen pre/post pairs.
Their preferred empirical link is standard normal, their robustness link is logistic, and their crime microfoundation separately yields a binomial-to-Poisson rare-event limit.
Their Gaussian weak-convergence proof requires the link density at inverse cell probabilities to be bounded away from zero, excluding probabilities drifting into a normal tail.
Fernández-Val, Meier, van Vuuren, and Vella (2024, arXiv:2409.02311) develop related distribution-regression DiD identification with covariates and multiple outcomes but do not analyze rare-tail link equivalence.
Wooldridge (2023, DOI 10.1093/ectj/utad016) develops nonlinear DiD with logit and Poisson QMLE and explicitly leaves transformation choice for further work.
Roth and Sant'Anna (2023, DOI 10.3982/ECTA19402) establish that functional-form sensitivity of parallel trends is an identification issue rather than a cosmetic modeling choice.
Athey and Imbens (2006, Econometrica) and Callaway and Li (2019, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2018.06.008) are foundational nonlinear and distributional DiD anchors but do not study rare-link cancellation.
Chernozhukov, Fernández-Val, Melly, and Wüthrich (2019, arXiv:1608.05142) provide distribution-function band inversion for discrete quantiles, not boundary inference for the rare underlying DF map.
Di Tella and Schargrodsky (2004, AER) supply the 37-treated-block Buenos Aires police experiment, whose sparse treated sample limits finite-sample power.
Baricz (2008, DOI 10.1016/j.jmaa.2007.09.063) and Pinelis (2019, arXiv:1512.00120) provide the closest analytic machinery for inverse-Mills signs and derivative remainders.
Chen and Fang (2019, arXiv:1901.04861) and Hong and Li (2018, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2018.06.007) cover first-order degeneracy and numerical second-order delta methods while retaining Gaussian base experiments.
Marohn (2001) shows that rare statistical experiments can switch between Gaussian and Poisson limits, furnishing an anchor for the nρ frontier.
Sachs, Gabriel, and Fay (2026, arXiv:2406.19141) give small-sample confidence inversion for functions of multinomial probabilities but not a deterministic rational certificate with a diameter theorem.
Arratia, Goldstein, and Gordon (1989, DOI 10.1214/aop/1176991491) and Ehm (1991, DOI 10.1016/0167-7152(91)90170-V) provide quantitative approximation tools for dependent and unequal rare counts.
The scan found no published theorem combining normal-link distributional-DiD cancellation, exact cancellation-plane uniformity, Gaussian/product-Poisson drifting limits, and certified zero-count-safe inference.

The failed eid_binary_did_scale_frontier/v1 supplied the closest link-scale predecessor; reviewers rejected algebra-only frontiers and requested an observable statistic, limit law, and decision rule.
The accepted panel_ppml_forbidden_comparison/v1 supplied primitive sign-frontier geometry; its rejected angle cores were inspected for unresolved global-frontier questions.

Its reviewer explicitly requested an unknown-intensity extension.
Its uniform-certificate question remains unresolved, and its honest scope excludes equality contacts, a uniform finite cover, and individual-data sufficiency.
The downgraded stat_pn_weak_event_honest_inference run supplied rare-event inversion and the rejected-angle question on post-selection event honesty.
No prior artifact establishes the common-cutoff inverse-Mills constants uniformly on both rare-link cancellation planes.
